summary: Bad taste merge. The actual move is 3 renames + a registry row insert + a few CLI/doc string updates — maybe 10 files. The PR is 44. Everything else is ceremony, stowaways, and unresolved duplication that should never have crossed review.

findings.title: Six .omc/.project-memory.json.tmp.<uuid> stowaways committed
findings.why: These are unmistakably tool scratch files — uuid-suffixed atomic-write tempfiles that should be unlinked on commit, not committed to history. Every reviewer who pulls this branch now has six dead files pretending to be tracked state. .gitignore does not exclude them; nothing does. This is the kind of slop that rots a repo.
findings.fix: Add `.omc/.project-memory.json.tmp.*` to .gitignore and `git rm` the six paths in a follow-up commit. Also fix whatever tool is leaking these — write-rename-unlink discipline, not write-rename-forget.

findings.title: Spec doc lives in two places; PR updates both instead of deleting one
findings.why: Two near-identical 21K files diverging by ~200 bytes. The PR touches BOTH with the same string rename, cementing the duplication instead of fixing it. A 'cleanup lane' PR that propagates a duplicate is not cleanup — it is maintenance debt with a green checkmark.
findings.fix: Pick one canonical path (docs/decisions/specs/ per ADR convention), delete the other, redirect any inbound links. Do it in this PR or open a follow-up issue and link it from the PR body.

findings.title: capability-record-template.yaml exists in two roots AND a -v2 sibling
findings.why: Three files, three different sizes, no versioning policy in the diff or PR body, no statement of which is canonical, no sunset date for v1, no ADR. A PR whose entire purpose is to 'centralize capability templates' that leaves three forks of the central template behind is contradicting its own headline. The `-v2` suffix is the sloppiest possible versioning convention: no ADR, no migration window, no removal date.
findings.fix: Either delete -v2 and amend v1 in place (with a version bump field inside the YAML), or sunset v1 with an ADR and delete it. Pick a canonical root: `templates/` OR `docs/templates/`, not both. State the policy in ADR-0116 or a new ADR.

findings.title: 5 ADR amendments bundled into a string-rename PR
findings.why: ADRs are append-only decision records. Silently editing five accepted ADRs to chase a path rename inside the SAME PR as the rename means there is no audit trail saying 'we renamed; here is what we touched in each ADR; here is why amending is preferred over a superseding ADR.' The PR body claims 'no new ADR added because this is a mechanical topology move' — but it is amending five existing ADRs, which IS an ADR change and deserves its own record or at minimum an explicit listing of the amended ADRs with rationale per file.
findings.fix: Either (a) split the ADR amendments into a follow-up PR with a meta-ADR explaining the mechanical-rename amendment policy, or (b) enumerate each amended ADR + diff rationale in the PR body and link to ADR-0116 explicitly from each amended ADR.

findings.title: PR body admits fmt + clippy were not run
evidence: ⚠️ cargo fmt --check → not run; this toolchain lacks the fmt subcommand
⚠️ cargo clippy → not run; this toolchain lacks the clippy subcommand
findings.why: A merged PR with two CI bars unexecuted because the local toolchain is broken is the author's problem, not the reviewer's. Either rustup the missing components or push to a branch and let remote CI do it before merging — do not merge with a shrug.
findings.fix: `rustup component add rustfmt clippy` for toolchain 1.95.0, rerun, paste output. Going forward, gate merge on remote CI not local verification.

findings.title: PR body says 'capability-reviewer / doc-style-reviewer pending' yet PR is merged
evidence: Per-change-class reviewer agent run: pending capability-reviewer / doc-style-reviewer on PR.
findings.why: Merging while declared reviewers are 'pending' makes the reviewer registry decorative. Either the reviewers are required or they are not; pick one and act consistently.
findings.fix: If the reviewers are required for CC-3, the merge button should have been blocked. If they are not required, remove the line from the PR template.

good_taste_signal: The actual code edit in crates/oya-dev-cli is small (lib.rs +3/-3, two gate files +1/-1) and looks like a clean string-constant pivot to the new registry path. That core is fine. Everything around it is the problem.

missing: No removal of the OLD path (PR claims it removes 'the empty retired directory' but the diff does not show the deletion line for the old fixture directory's .gitkeep or equivalent — verify the prior location is actually gone, not just empty)
No CI lane added to prevent regrowth (lean-a-foundry-capability-template-registry is named in the PR body but no .github/workflows or lane definition appears in the diff)
No backward-compat shim or sunset note for consumers reading the old path
No statement on what happens if a downstream tool has the old path string hard-coded

linus_take: Show me the patch and I will tell you if you have good taste. This patch has bad taste. Move 3 files, update some strings, done — 10 files, one commit, one PR. Instead this is 44 files with stowaways, duplicates, and ADR drive-bys. The core change is fine; the packaging is sloppy. Reject, split, resubmit.
recommendation: REJECT and split into: (1) the actual rename + registry row + CLI string update + ADR-0116 ref (~10 files), (2) ADR-000X / ADR amendments PR with explicit rationale, (3) duplicate-spec dedup PR, (4) capability-record-template canonicalization PR with policy, (5) chore PR to add .omc tempfile gitignore + delete stowaways.
